summary: More than 12,000 Munduruku live around Brazil’s Tapajós River, which supports their food supply, transportation and cultural practices. After the proposed São Luiz do Tapajós dam was denied following opposition from the Munduruku, Greenpeace and supporters, 40 other dams remain planned for the basin. Seeking official recognition and protection of their territory, the Munduruku created a “Map of Life” depicting sacred places and essential resources. They delivered it to Brazil’s Ministry of Justice during an Indigenous rights mobilisation. More than 1.2 million people have signed a petition supporting them.
